blind_spots_patched: Baseline Chapter 6 praised 132.4% FY2025 CFO/NI conversion without auditing refundable/offsettable customer temporary receipts, government grant PP&E offsets masking GAAP depreciation, working capital divergence, or the non-cash VIS remeasurement gain.

Baseline Chapter 4 discussed Taiwan Strait risk broadly while omitting statutory Section 232/301 tariff rules, the Dec 2025 expiration of TSMC Nanjing's VEU waiver, quantified USD/NTD operating-margin sensitivity, FX forward losses, and the Nov 12 employee-data breach.
Baseline Chapter 6 assumed zero strategic equity investing outside cleanrooms and omitted statutory profit-sharing formulas, the 1987 ITRI 35% government capacity clause, and SSMC take-or-pay floors.
Baseline Chapter 2 left Q3 2026 platform and geographic shares as vague placeholders and omitted the sharp 2026 shift toward U.S.-headquartered clients and surging non-wafer packaging revenue.
assumptions_changed: CONFIRMED: Q3 2026 revenue reached US$46.72B (NT$1,494.24B) with HPC dominant (>65%) and leading-edge nodes (<=7nm) at 79% of wafer sales.
CONFIRMED: October 2026 sales rose 59.7% YoY to NT$586.89B, validating Q4 2026 guidance and management's steady capital-return and capacity discipline.
WEAKENED: TSMC avoids M&A and deploys retained cash strictly into cleanrooms, EUV tools, R&D, and dividends, preserving a ~$66B net cash fortress.
CONFIRMED: Overseas fab expansions (Arizona, Kumamoto, Dresden) are cushioned by sovereign CHIPS Act subsidies and multi-year LTA customer prepayments.
CONFIRMED: Taiwan Strait geopolitics, top-customer concentration, and overseas fab margin drag (2%-4%) represent the primary structural vulnerabilities.
